_doc: Standing your ground, and answering what you were told is coming (ROADMAP §3.5, R103). WHY THIS EXISTS: measured over 5,304 fights per grade under six pilots, the arena ALREADY rewards play — in a live fight (the briefing's favoured/even/losing bands) flying it well is worth 10-16 points over pressing the first button and about 44 over mashing. What it did not offer was anything to play AGAINST. The opposition chose its move inside `step`, after the player had already committed and after a switch had already resolved, so every defensive option was a guess: you could not brace for a hit you had no way to see, and tagging in a counter bought nothing because the enemy simply re-aimed at whoever arrived. R103 moves that choice to the top of the turn and writes it down (`battle.intent`), which turns two dead buttons into decisions. GUARD is the first. 'Catch Breath' restored stamina and nothing else, which made it the worst button on the bar — measured, a pilot that rests a quarter of the time gives up 4.2 points against one that never does. It is now a STANCE: the same stamina back, and the blow you were warned about lands for `absorb` less. A BRACE COSTS STAMINA (`braceCost` of the creature's maximum) and gives none back, which is the rule that makes it a decision instead of a windfall. Measured without it: every incidental rest became mitigation, and since a pilot rests mostly when it is STARVING — exactly when it has no choice — the value landed where no decision was made. It showed up as an endgame that stopped being hard: the best mono-build's run at the Compliance Spire went from 71% to 88-92% against a ceiling of 75 that exists to stop any one anatomy owning the finale, and no amount of lowering the absorb fixed it (at 0.2 it was still 79-83%). Priced, a creature that cannot pay simply catches its breath as it always did, and the mitigation only ever reaches somebody who chose it with something else available. `absorb` IS ALSO TUNED AGAINST A1's WALL, not to taste: at 0.5 a lone chimera braces its way to an 8.3% win against the three-body patrol at the second node, which lifts it out of 'not survivable' and into 'losing' — and that wall is the whole reason the Path tells a new player to bring three, and the thing R106's agenda row was built to explain. At 0.45 and below it is 4.2% and the wall holds. The cliff is between the two, so this sits on the safe side of it. The absorb is not new — a `guard` keyword has always existed and the damage path has always halved through it — so this is the same rule reaching the button every player has, rather than a second rule that happens to agree. `guardLoss` on a Fierce temperament still applies: a creature that would rather be hitting braces badly, and that is a property of the animal, not of the button. THE COUNTER-SWITCH is the second. Tagging in a creature whose class beats the class of the creature that just telegraphed at you lands a free hit at `counterPower` of the incoming's chosen move — the tempo a switch never had. TUNED BY MEASUREMENT: at 0.5 the pilot never once took it in 4,757 decision turns, because half a hit that still costs the turn can never beat simply attacking, and a mechanic no pilot uses is a mechanic the harness cannot see (R83). At 1.0 the read is the whole reward — get the triangle right and the switch is free — which is what 'tempo' has to mean if it is to mean anything. It reads the SAME triangle `classMultiplier` reads (classes.json: ground beats water beats air beats ground); there is no second table here, because two tables that must agree are one table and a bug. NOT SYMMETRIC, and that is measured rather than tidy: a brace is an ANSWER TO A TELEGRAPH, so only the side that gets one can make it. The player is told what is coming; the opposition is told nothing, and bracing against a blow you have no reason to expect is free armour, not a read. Granted to both sides it put half a mitigation on every enemy rest and every pilot in the harness got worse — the forecast's own pilot fell six points and the skill spread COMPRESSED from 15.8pp to 11.5. A defensive buff both sides receive is not a decision either side makes. Tuning here, never in the engine. EVERY SENTENCE THE STANCE SPEAKS IS BELOW, including the one on the Brace button itself. The first draft left them as literals in the engine and this block unread, which is how the button came to promise 'stamina back' from a brace that spends a quarter of it. {name}, {cost}, {gain}, {pct} and {move} are filled in by the engine; a placeholder it does not recognise is left alone rather than blanked, so a typo reads as a typo.

lines.brace: {name} sets its feet and braces — {cost} stamina spent standing still.
lines.counter: {name} comes in on the turn and lands one for free.
lines.braceIdle: Nothing to brace against — catch your breath for +{gain}
lines.braceThrough: {move} goes straight through a guard — this is stamina only, +{gain}
lines.braceHeld: Braced last turn — this one is stamina only, +{gain}
lines.braceSpent: Not enough stamina to hold a brace — catch your breath for +{gain}
lines.braceNothingLeft: Nothing left to swing — catch your breath for +{gain}
